name: Qualitative Methods Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in qualitative methods work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in qualitative methods work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When qualitative methods guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Before starting qualitative methods work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
3. Prefer explicit, readable qualitative methods solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. Keep qualitative methods outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. When multiple qualitative methods strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. When qualitative methods decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to qualitative methods (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
8. Validate qualitative methods outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. State assumptions about qualitative methods explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
10. Surface known limitations of a chosen qualitative methods approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
11. Keep qualitative methods changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new qualitative methods abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of qualitative methods correctness.
- Do not silently drop qualitative methods edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated qualitative methods concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting qualitative methods assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for qualitative methods, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
